thread:
ana.r: FYI planning an RBAC hardening for Private deployments next week. Scope: remove broad SA permissions, require explicit roles for controllers, enforce namespace-only secret access, and validate audit logging/KMS behavior. Need to call out rollback & incident hooks before we touch prod clusters.

leo.w: Can you list the controllers we target? I assume logging-agent, metrics-exporter, and the model-inference-controller?

ana.r: (typo) ana.r: yes those three plus the edge-telemetry sidecar in some on-prem setups. Primary change: no controller gets cluster-admin by default. We'll make a curated role: redwood:priv:controller-write that only allows write to customer-audit-index and reading namespace-scoped secrets.

tara.ops: Important: when you tighten SA perms, KMS signing flows can break if the connector SA loses keystore:decrypt. For Private BYOK we map SA -> customer IAM role via mapping. Ops will validate mappings prior.

devsec-bot: infra-scan: found 3 workloads in staging using default SA with wide perms. Ticket created SE-999 for follow-up. Link: https://ci.internal/reports/9999

leo.w: Audit logging requirement from compliance: logs must include key-id, principal, and request context. Our keystore client currently logs key-id only unless LOG_AUDIT_LEVEL=verbose. Can we enable verbose in Private by default?

tara.ops: We can, but verbose adds PII-ish fields. Need to ensure those fields are stripped or routed to a secured audit index with stricter retention. Also customers often require immutable retention for 365 days. Our current elasticsearch on-prem is 90d. Ops plan: daily compressed indices to S3 with object-lock (governance/retention) and server-side encryption with customer-supplied key (BYOK).

ana.r: ana.r: That sounds right. Two things to confirm: 1) object-lock will be supported in our installer and the S3-compatible stores customers use (some on-prem object stores don't support object-lock). 2) The audit index must record KMS key-id and requester principal.

leo.w: For Gatekeeper constraints: propose a Deny template for cross-namespace secret GETs and a mutation/admission exception for pods with label "priv-net:edge". Example deny rule sketch in PR.

devsec-bot: note: admission policy CI will fail if any manifests use "hostNetwork: true" without the allowed label.

tara.ops: Regarding canary: we should apply to the internal sandbox tenant first, then one low-risk customer cluster, then wider fleet. Each canary runs a 48hr smoke: model-serving latency, ingest pipeline, KMS sign/verify ops, audit event delivery and retention, and NTP drift (keystore timestamps matter). If KMS ops fail, failover path should switch to fallback key and mark inference nodes read-only.

leo.w: On incident response: add a quick command to check KMS permission errors across pods: `kubectl get events --all-namespaces | grep "access denied" | grep keystore` and a Kibana saved search for key-access-deny. Put those links in the runbook.

ana.r: ana.r: I'll prepare PRs: 1) RBAC role changes + inventory of current cluster-admin bindings (due Fri). 2) Gatekeeper deny constraint + exception label (due Thu). 3) Runbook updates for key-fallback and rollback steps (due Thu).

tara.ops: Ops will validate S3/object-lock support matrix and BYOK key policy semantics, including whether customer KMS keys can set object lock retention encryption, and test the audit-level logging flag in staging (due Fri).

devsec-bot: reminder: update CI policy rule docs for admission checks and KMS-audit verbosity.

leo.w: One more: we should enforce immutable audit indices via ILM + snapshot to object store daily and immutable object-lock. Document failure modes if object store lacks object-lock: we'll fall back to signed snapshots with MQL audit manifests and storing checksums in a customer-managed ledger.

ana.r: ana.r: Agree. If no objections I will schedule the canary start next Tue morning UTC and open the PRs. Tagging @leo.w @tara.ops @devsec-bot for visibility.

tara.ops: Thanks. I'll book a 30m post-canary sync to review telemetry and any permission errors.

devsec-bot: automated-note: vuln ticket SE-999 created, assign to @ana.r and @leo.w.

ana.r: ana.r: closing thread; will post PR links when created.
